messages:
sajal: RFC follow-up: per-prefix version vectors for ownership safety. proposing we attach a tiny version vector to prefix metadata so caches can detect stale residency after handoff. sketch below.
rachel: quick q — what invariant are we trying to preserve exactly?
sajal: avoid this: nodeA caches prefix P, handoff to nodeB, nodeB serves newer writes but nodeA still replies from stale KV for a short time. need deterministic rejection of stale cache reads.
tom: my immediate worry: vector size and perf. we already store epoch + lease; adding vectors per-prefix could bloat memory.
eli: can we make it opportunistic? only track multi-node handoffs where affinity changes, otherwise keep single epoch. maybe compress to 1-2 entries.
marie: should we consider a compacted representation: small bitmap or hashed id + counter pair instead of full map? saves bytes at the cost of probabilistic collision.
sajal: yes, goal is tiny. proposal: version vector encoded as list of (node_short_id, uint32 counter). default is single entry: owner_id:epoch. on handoff, new owner increments its counter and publishes vector with handshake. readers reject cached reply if their seen vector is older in lexicographic compare.
rachel: how do we compare when vectors have different membership? standard vv partial order may be inconclusive. what's the fallback?
sajal: if incomparable -> conservative path: miss/read-through to authoritative store. only pay cost in ambiguous cases (rare).
tom: can we detect common fast path: when both vectors are single-entry and owner id matches, compare counters -> cheap. only multi-owner vectors go to slow path.
eli: what about write amplification? we need to persist vector updates with each handoff. handoffs are relatively rare vs tokens churn, so OK. but we must avoid updating vector on every short-lived prefetch.
marie: telemetry idea: add metric prefix.version_vector.size and prefix.vv.incomparable_count so we know how often we hit slow path.
infra-bot: CI run triggered: https://ci.redwood/changes/PR-rr-vv-1764 (unit + microbench queued).
sajal: API change sketch (proto):
```proto
message PrefixVersionVector {
  repeated uint32 node_ids = 1; // short ids (<= 65535)
  repeated uint32 counters = 2;
}
message PrefixMetadata {
  string prefix = 1;
  PrefixVersionVector vv = 10;
  // other fields...
}
```
eli: encoding nit: use delta-encoded counters in wire to save bytes when counters are small. also cap vector length to 4 entries.
rachel: rollout plan? we need backward compat with older nodes that don't understand vv.
sajal: graceful: new nodes publish vv, old nodes ignore unknown field. on reads, if server sees unknown vv from client, treat as missing -> conservative read-through. we can enable VV check in two-phase rollout: control plane flag to opt-in namespaces.
tom: can we avoid changing on-disk layout? stick vv into dynamic metadata blob to avoid format churn.
sajal: yes, put vv in opaque metadata field to start. later migration to typed field if stable.
marie: ops playbook: when vv.incomparable_count spikes, run a prefix-ownership audit and look for frequent flip-flops. could be a symptom of noisy scheduler.
eli: tests to add: fuzz handoff race where nodeA serves cached reply during simultaneous commit on nodeB; assert client never observes older/violating sequence.
rachel: ok, would love a small perf sim showing average added bytes per-prefix and slow-path rate.
sajal: will run a simulation on the hotset trace for last 7 days. I'll post numbers here. thanks all for feedback — updated doc: https://rwd.in/internal/prefix-vv-draft (WIP)
marie: :thumbsup: keep the proto tiny and add the telemetry.
eli: another follow-up — consider GC for vv entries: evict non-owner entries after N handoffs to keep vector compact.
sajal: good point. add TTL heuristic and a max-entries cap in the proposal.
marie: sgtm.
infra-bot: link to perf job: https://perf.redwood/job/1764-vv-sim (queued).
